title: Petra and the Bell
premise: Noor Whitlock takes a routine appraisal of Bellhaven House, a hillside property whose founders vanished in 1911 after ringing a bronze bell over a dry well. The house's mirrors begin lagging a second behind reality, and the reflections start acting independently, showing Noor versions of rooms that no longer exist. She discovers the founders' unfinished ritual: the bell must be rung thirteen times at the well's edge before the well refills with what drowned there, or the house will claim a new keeper. As Noor's own reflection begins living her life one second ahead, she learns loyalty to the house's last surviving descendant is a lie built on her forgotten childhood spent inside its walls. In the end, Noor rings the twelfth toll herself and lets her reflection ring the thirteenth, trading her memory of the house for survival — and walks out unable to remember why her hands smell of bronze.
about_author: Wren Halloran is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent a decade cataloguing condemned properties across New England. Their fiction grows from the conviction that every old house keeps an inventory of everyone who ever tried to leave it.

chapters.title: The Square Footage of Silence
chapters.summary: Noor arrives at Bellhaven House to appraise it, noting its immaculate condition despite decades vacant. Her instruments give impossible readings; the tape measure shortens itself. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination as the house seems to notice her.

chapters.title: Thirteen Rooms, Twelve Doors
chapters.summary: Noor counts doors on her survey and gets twelve where blueprints promise thirteen. A neighbor, Elias Vann, warns her off before dusk. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the first crack in her rationalism as arithmetic becomes something the house can argue with.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: At night in the empty house, every mirror reflects the room a full second late. Noor tests it with a dropped coin and watches her reflection catch it before she does. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into scientific denial she knows is failing.

chapters.title: The Descendant
chapters.summary: Maren Bell, great-granddaughter of the founders, appears claiming the estate and asks Noor to stay through the appraisal week. Her warmth feels rehearsed. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: charm laid over desperation, revealing Maren needs Noor for reasons unspoken.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Founders
chapters.summary: In the cellar archive, Noor finds the 1911 ledger: Aldous and Ivy Bell's notes on a ritual of thirteen tolls over the well, abandoned at twelve. The final page names 'a keeper who remembers.' POV: Noor. Emotional beat: discovery mixed with the chill of being expected.

chapters.title: What the Well Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor finds the capped well behind the garden wall; frost blooms around it in summer heat. Something below answers when she knocks. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: terror tempered by a strange homesickness she cannot explain.

chapters.title: Reflections Ahead
chapters.summary: The mirrors now show the future: Noor's reflection rings a bell she hasn't touched. Maren dismisses it too quickly. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing, hinting Maren has seen this before with someone else.

chapters.title: Elias's Testimony
chapters.summary: Elias reveals he was the surveyor sent in 1987; his partner stayed past the week and never left. He gives Noor his old notes and begs her to leave by Friday. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: survivor's shame, and the cost of walking away made flesh.

chapters.title: Rooms That Were
chapters.summary: Following her reflection, Noor passes through the thirteenth door into rooms from 1911, furnished and lit, where a woman resembling her sets a table. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: vertigo of recognition — the woman turns, and Noor flees before seeing her face.

chapters.title: The Missing Week
chapters.summary: Digging into county records, Noor finds herself listed as a resident of Bellhaven House at age six, a year she cannot remember. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: identity fracturing; the house didn't choose her, it kept her.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered, Maren admits the family bargain: each generation sends a keeper to finish the ritual, and Maren's mother failed. Maren chose Noor deliberately. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: betrayal and pity entwined — Maren weeps even as she lies about the rest.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor prepares to flee but finds her car's engine full of well water. The house has closed its inventory around her. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: rage giving way to grim resolve — if she cannot leave, she will finish what the Bells started.

chapters.title: The Rite of Tolls
chapters.summary: From the ledger, Noor reconstructs the ritual: thirteen tolls at the well's edge before the equinox tide refills it, each toll paid for with a memory. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: cold clarity — she maps which memories she can afford to lose.

chapters.title: First Toll
chapters.summary: Noor rings the bell once; the memory of her mother's face dissolves. The well exhales, and the mirrors align perfectly for one breathless moment. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: grief and power together — the price works, and part of her is glad to pay.

chapters.title: Tolls Two Through Six
chapters.summary: Montage of losses: her college years, her sister's voice, her reason for becoming a surveyor. Each toll, the house grows warmer, more welcoming. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: seduction of forgetting — the house offers peace with every payment.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Table
chapters.summary: At the seventh toll, the thirteenth room opens fully, and Noor meets the woman from 1911: Ivy Bell, alive in the house's memory, who mistakes Noor for her lost daughter. POV: alternating Noor/Ivy. Emotional beat: tenderness inside horror — Ivy's love is real and it is a trap.

chapters.title: Ivy's Warning
chapters.summary: Ivy breaks free of the loop long enough to warn Noor: the twelfth toll belongs to the keeper, but the thirteenth must be rung by someone willing — and the well chooses who it makes willing. POV: Ivy. Emotional beat: maternal sacrifice across a century, and the first true ally Noor has had.

chapters.title: Maren at the Edge
chapters.summary: Maren tries to take the bell and ring all thirteen herself, believing sacrifice will redeem her line. The well rejects her, dragging her toward the cap. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: ambition collapsing into terror as the house refuses her blood.

chapters.title: Tolls Eight Through Eleven
chapters.summary: Noor saves Maren and rings on, losing her name for the house, her memory of leaving it, her memory of choosing to stay. The walls begin to sweat and breathe. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: hollowing out — she continues on pure stubbornness, the last loyal thing she owns.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Toll
chapters.summary: Noor raises the bell for the twelfth time as the well uncaps itself below. Her reflection steps out of the mirror and takes the bell from her hands. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: surrender — she finally sees the face from the thirteenth room, and it is her own.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Toll
chapters.summary: Her reflection rings the final toll willingly, sealing the well and collapsing the thirteenth room into silence. The house exhales; Ivy Bell's loop ends with a smile. POV: the reflection. Emotional beat: release — two lives reconciled into one exit.

chapters.title: Appraisal Complete
chapters.summary: Noor signs her report on an empty, ordinary house, unable to remember the week or why her hands smell of bronze. Elias meets her at the gate; neither speaks of it. In her pocket: a brass bell clapper she doesn't recognize. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: survival purchased with memory, and the quiet horror of not knowing what it cost.
